### Rethinking Local News: How Sarah Alvarez Is Building Journalism in Support of Community Needs
Source: Nieman Reports
Published: 2026-11-11 13:00 UTC
URL: https://niemanreports.org/local-news-detroit-michigan-public-media-sarah-alvarez-founder-ceo-community-needs-foreclosures-outlier-media-documenters-city-bureau-chicago/

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Nieman Reports [media_lens] https://niemanreports.org/local-news-detroit-michigan-public-media-sarah-alvarez-founder-ceo-community-needs-foreclosures-outlier-media-documenters-city-bureau-chicago/

Sarah Alvarez has spent much of her career rethinking how local journalism can serve the public. After working as a civil rights attorney, then as a reporter and producer at the NPR station Michigan Public, she founded Outlier Media in 2016. Alvarez said the Detroit-based nonprofit newsroom was designed to fill information and accountability gaps in communities that were often overlooked by traditional news organizations.. One of its signature innovations, TXT OUTLIER, is a text message service Alvarez created to connect Detroiters directly with journalists and provide practical information on issues affecting their lives, from utility bills to housing and foreclosures. Under Alvarez’s leadership, Outlier also expanded its Documenters program, an initiative that trains and pays residents to attend and report on public meetings to create a public record of local government decisions in places that don’t have press coverage. The initiative has engaged more than 700 Detroiters and since spread nationwide, creating new opportunities for civic participation and public accountability.

With the first U.S. midterm elections since President Donald Trump’s return to the White House approaching, voters will be weighing in on a range of issues, from the economy and rising cost of living, to the administration’s foreign policy and the future direction of both major parties. At a recent virtual Nieman-to-Nieman seminar, a group of Nieman alums who cover politics discussed what they’re hearing from voters with regards to key Senate races, the growing influence of younger voters drawn to progressive candidates, and the political implications of conflicts involving Iran, Ukraine, and Russia. Moderated by Austin Bogues (NF ’21), news desk editor at USA Today, the discussion brought together James Barragán (NF ’24), political anchor for Spectrum News in Austin, Texas; Bill Barrow (NF ’22), national politics reporter for The Associated Press in Atlanta; and Ines Pohl (NF ’05), Washington bureau chief and White House correspondent for Deutsche Welle, Germany’s international public broadcaster.

As protests continue across India over allegations of government corruption, dozens of members of the media have been subjected to arrest, detainment and assault, according to witnesses, press rights organizations, and the journalists themselves. Thousands of protesters have taken to the streets of New Delhi in recent weeks, demanding the resignation of election officials allegedly tied to the deletion of nearly 130 million names from voter registration rolls. The protests — which have largely been organized by the Cockroach Janata Party, so named after India's chief justice called the nation’s unemployed youth and activists "cockroaches" — are part of a wider wave of youth discontent aimed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his administration. Organizers have mobilized young people via social media, tapping into frustrations with government corruption, eroding trust in democratic institutions, and a lack of access to jobs and educational opportunities.

The Trump administration’s latest attacks on the news media have followed a familiar pattern: President Donald Trump lashes out at news outlets for perceived bias and follows up with restrictive actions that appear blatantly unconstitutional; a judge’s ruling follows, temporarily halting the actions; and the administration pivots and pushes ahead with other restrictions. This time it was the removal of three outlets — CNN, MS NOW, and Politico — from White House press access in September. After the groups sued, and U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly issued a temporary restraining order restoring their access on Sept. 24, the administration barred CNN and Politico from providing pool coverage on trips outside Washington. Kelly issued a longer, preliminary injunction on Oct. 14, halting the administration from blocking the news organizations’ access to the White House while the case proceeds. Source: Nieman Reports

My happiest times in journalism have been when I have built something new. For my latest venture, I want to help bring investigative journalism on climate and environmental issues to a much larger audience than it has reached in the past. To do so, I’m starting a brand-new newsroom focused on the environmental and climate crisis, and I’m taking my audience along for the ride. I’ll be documenting every facet of the process with an “open kitchen” approach of radical transparency, starting with a 100-day video countdown chronicling all the steps involved with starting a news organization from the ground up. This effort combines two of the things I’m most passionate about: I love digging up stories that other people don’t want to see published, and I love creating opportunities for other journalists. I’ve been a journalist for most of my life. I started working at age 14 for the local paper in my rural German town, turned to doing investigative stories in my early 20s, and later studied investigative journalism at the Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism in New York.

### America’s Shrinking Local Newsrooms, Through a Photographer’s Lens
Source: Nieman Reports
Published: 2026-10-02 12:30 UTC
URL: https://niemanreports.org/americas-shrinking-local-newsrooms-photographer-ann-hermes-local-news-news-deserts-rural-america/
Source meta: reference_tool · aggregator · R3 · P4 · reference

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Nieman Reports [media_lens] https://niemanreports.org/americas-shrinking-local-newsrooms-photographer-ann-hermes-local-news-news-deserts-rural-america/

For many journalists, the sight of empty desks is a sadly familiar one. My first glimpse of a gutted newsroom facing further cutbacks sparked a documentary photography project that has so far taken me to more than 50 newsrooms across the United States over the past eight years. It began when my mother, a loyal subscriber to our local metro in southern Illinois, told me a decade ago how disappointed she was in the newspaper. She complained that the local coverage was lacking, and the paper seemed to be thinner. Already several years into my photojournalism career, I was unsurprised by her remarks — I had been witnessing the decline of print media since graduation from journalism school. Still, my curiosity was piqued, and I arranged a visit to the paper to see for myself. Cue the scene of a barren newsroom. Not only were there empty desks, but also an expanse of exposed carpet with indentations showing where desks had once long stood. While there has been a great deal of reporting on the issues plaguing local journalism, I hadn’t seen the story told visually.

[Premium Times] ₦210 trillion is not missing, we are told. It is merely unexplained. To an accountant, that is not comforting at all.This week, former NNPC Group Chief Executive Mele Kyari again insisted that no ₦210 trillion was lost under his watch, describing the disputed figures as bookkeeping issues. ### 澳枪击事件嫌疑人为父子：曾宣誓效忠“伊斯兰国”，行凶枪支为合法持有
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-16 02:23 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178049
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178049

据新华社12月15日援引澳大利亚广播公司报道，澳大利亚联合反恐小组调查人员表示，悉尼邦迪滩枪击事件两名嫌疑人曾宣誓效忠“伊斯兰国”恐怖组织。 报道援引联合反恐小组一名不愿透露姓名的高级官员的话说，警方在邦迪滩两名枪手车内发现一面“伊斯兰国”旗帜。澳大利亚安全情报组织6年前就已在调查邦迪滩枪击案两名枪手之一的纳维德·阿克拉姆，他与“伊斯兰国”在悉尼的恐怖分子有密切联系。 澳大利亚警方表示，枪击事件的两名嫌疑人是父子关系，使用合法获得的枪支发动了此次袭击事件。 澳大利亚总理阿尔巴尼斯15日表示：“今天下午4点， 我将把更严格的枪支法律列入国家内阁的议程，包括限制个人可持有或许可的枪支数量 。此外，还需对许可证进行定期审查。人们的情况会发生变化，人们的思想也会随着时间的推移而变得激进。许可证不应永久有效。” 此次枪击事件已造成包括1名作案嫌疑人在内的16人死亡、40人受伤。这是自1996年塔斯马尼亚州亚瑟港枪击事件造成35人死亡以来，澳大利亚发生的最严重的大规模枪击事件。 持有枪支许可证长达十年 据多家外媒报道，其中一名袭击者为24岁的澳大利亚公民纳维德·阿克拉姆，他在现场被捕，随后被送往悉尼的一家医院。另一名袭击者是他的父亲萨吉德·阿克拉姆，他于1998年来到澳大利亚，被警方当场击毙。 澳大利亚警方随后证实，纳维德·阿克拉姆此前已被新南威尔士州警方和其他机构记录在案。其父亲萨吉德·阿克拉姆持有枪支许可证，名下登记有6支枪，目前均已被追回。新南威尔士州警察局长马尔·兰永透露，萨吉德·阿克拉姆已持有枪支许可证长达十年。 阿尔巴尼斯在新闻发布会上透露，纳维德·阿克拉姆曾于2019年10月首次引起当局的注意。他补充说，对该男子进行检查是基于他与其他人有联系，但评估结果表明，没有任何迹象表明他存在持续的威胁或暴力倾向。 新南威尔士州州长克里斯·明斯表示，警方正在调查他们的系统是否存在故障，导致合法持有的武器可能被用于恐怖袭击。 枪手“性格古怪”，爱好打猎 据《卫报》澳大利亚版报道，纳维德·阿克拉姆在袭击前从事砌砖工作。他的同事表示，纳维德性格古怪，“没人和他亲近”。“（砌砖工人）在一起的时间很长，因为砌砖是一项非常枯燥乏味的工作，所以大家会聊很多话。但纳维德是一个性格很古怪的人……他工作非常努力，几乎没有休息日。” 尽管澳大利亚警方并未确认纳维德·阿克拉姆是否合法持有枪支，但据这位同事表示，纳维德经常外出打猎，曾提及在昆士兰州南部高原的克鲁克韦尔附近射杀兔子和其他猎物。这位同事还表示，就在几周前，纳维德告诉老板，他的手骨折了，所以要到2026年才能工作。

### 儿童手表“小天才圈”调查：点赞成每日功课，有商家可解除家长管控
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-15 14:23 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32177210
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32177210

在校园里，孩子们时常举起戴在手腕上的手表，彼此一碰，便加为好友。 这种以“安全”为核心卖点的儿童电话手表，如今已超越通信工具的属性，悄然演变成一个拥有独特规则、社交层级甚至灰色产业链的未成年人数字社交圈——“小天才圈”。 在这个属于他们的“江湖”里，“大佬榜”备受关注，“扩列”（增加好友）成为新的社交需求，“点主”（在主页点赞）是每日必做的功课……这些让成年人感到陌生的词汇，正构筑着未成年人的数字社交世界。 然而，伴随着这种社交形态的兴起，家长们的担忧也日益加剧：孩子过度沉迷手表社交、不良信息传播、因品牌壁垒导致的“社交绑架”等问题逐渐浮现。《法治日报》记者近日对该现象展开调查，试图揭开这一未成年人数字社交圈的真实面貌。 点赞成社交“硬通货” 据北京“小天才圈”资深玩家陈曦（化名）介绍，圈内有5000余名活跃用户，多为11岁至17岁的学生，这个社交圈形成了一套精心设计的“混圈规则”。“入圈”需设定两个字的独特圈名，随后可在平台分享生活点滴，吸引具有相同爱好的好友进行互动；若想提升知名度或影响力，需每日经营主页并与好友动态互动。 记者注意到，在一些社交平台上，大量以“小天才圈交友攻略”为主题的内容应运而生，内容涵盖如何快速“扩列”、获取更多点赞等“实用”技巧，评论区有不少“留下ID互加好友”的留言。在这一社交体系中，点赞是这套规则的核心——平台设定每日主页获赞上限为3000个，若要达到“100万+”的“大佬”级别，需连续点赞近一年时间。围绕点赞数与知名度，圈内形成了清晰的“大佬排行榜”，点赞数也成为社交“硬通货”。 这种对点赞的追逐，已催生出相关服务产业。记者调查发现，某社交平台上，拥有数十万甚至上百万点赞数的账号，售价从几百元到上千元不等：100多万点赞的账号标价1300元，90多万点赞的账号标价1200元。 今年18岁的“灵师”（圈名），在2021年14岁时加入“小天才圈”，她的账号目前已拥有150个好友、超100万点赞量。她告诉记者，这样的账号市场价值约1000元。 “围绕点赞需求，还衍生出代刷赞、租账号、出售‘大佬好友位’等服务。”“灵师”进一步介绍，例如付费100元至180元，即可获得“bot”（记者注：“bot”是一种第三方开发的自动化工具，主要用于刷赞、修改记录和发送动态等功能，这类工具能帮助用户快速提升账号点赞数，从而在未成年人社交圈中获得更高地位）自动点赞功能——用户将手表寄给相关人员进行10天左右的处理便能完成安装。此后，发帖5分钟内即可自动获赞，还可以一键查询未点赞名单。

近日，总台接到群众举报，反映陈皮市场存在年份虚标、产地及工艺造假等问题，千元一斤的“年份陈皮”亦可能名不副实。 茶枝柑新果皮冒充陈皮 广西浦北出现“速成工艺陈皮” 记者发现，直播间里售卖陈皮低价轮番轰炸，年份承诺掷地有声。 直播间也有主播爆料，八成市面上所谓广东新会陈皮实为广西陈皮。 广西钦州市浦北县是茶枝柑重要种植基地，其果皮是陈皮风味“越陈越香”关键，也是浦北陈皮唯一原料。2024年当地陈皮产业产值破60亿元，采收季大量鲜果加工晾晒成柑皮。 果农和收购商称，今年浦北茶枝柑鲜果收购价走低。按20斤鲜果出1斤柑皮比例，叠加人工成本，品相好的新柑皮成本约30元/斤，低端柑皮仅六七元，且当年新柑皮并非真正陈皮。 这家企业的负责人告诉记者，按行业共识与团体标准，柑皮需陈化三年以上才可称为陈皮，陈化时间越长价值越高，但他透露，自然陈化需长期积压资金，多数企业是难以承受的。 这家企业的负责人私下告诉记者，为缓解资金占用压力，一种名为“轻工艺”的速成加工方式，眼下正在部分陈皮生产企业里流行，他们仅需一个月的时间，就能将新采收的茶枝柑果皮处理为外观近似三年、五年自然陈化过的陈皮，这样做能大幅缩短陈化周期、降低企业的运营成本。 浦北自然陈化五年陈皮批发价每斤150元至200元，企业造假“工艺皮”成本仅70元左右，高额利润促使更多商家放弃自然陈化、铤而走险。 记者离开企业，在广西浦北县柑浦堂健康产业有限公司分拣车间，再次见到大批量造假“工艺皮”陈皮，同一批“工艺皮”因加工受热差异形成色差，被分拣标注为三年、五年等不同年份。 负责人透露，不同年份“工艺皮”本质相同，批发价均70元左右一斤，零售价差极大，标五年款卖500元一斤，标十年款卖1000元一斤，仅凭外观就能翻倍抬价，利润超成本十倍以上。 新会陈皮从浦北进货 “工艺皮”贴上陈皮标签以假乱真 浦北与新会陈皮原料同为茶枝柑，仅产地不同，新会较高生产成本使当地部分头部商家常年从浦北拿货，浦北成其重要原料供应地。 记者在柑浦堂分拣仓库看到，大量标注“新会陈皮”“新会特产”的纸箱正打包“工艺皮”，这些广西陈皮每日批量发往广东新会，造假供需链路已成熟稳定。 记者发现，浦北当地部分规模企业和小型收购商，已形成了这种“工艺皮”的造假供应体系，可自主加工或快速调配各类“年份”陈皮货品，个别企业年销新会原料数量惊人。 随后经浦北陈皮企业负责人引荐，记者见到多位专程从新会赴浦北采购的商家，他们坦言同时经营新会皮与浦北皮，外地“工艺皮”因价格低廉成电商供货重要选择。

### 《怦然心动》导演莱纳与妻子在家中遇害，警方尚未证实是其子所杀
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻

Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline

当地时间12月14日，曾执导《怦然心动》《当哈利遇到莎莉》《危情十日》等影片的美国导演罗伯·莱纳（Rob Reiner）在他位于洛杉矶的家中遇害身亡。洛杉矶警察已对外证实，现年78岁的莱纳与他现年68岁的妻子米歇尔·辛格·莱纳（Michele Singer Reiner）的遗体一同被发现。 2019年，罗伯·莱纳（左一）与《当哈利遇到莎莉》的主演梅格·瑞恩、比利·克里斯托出席TMC经典电影节。 据悉，洛杉矶消防局的人员于当地时间12月14日下午3点38分接到医疗救助电话，赶赴位于布伦特伍德区的一处住宅中，随后发现两人已死亡。当天晚间，洛杉矶警察局在其社交媒体官方账号确认死者为导演罗伯·莱纳夫妇，将由抢劫凶杀部门主导调查。而好莱坞媒体TMZ援引执法部门消息称，“两人身上有与刀具造成的伤口相符的割裂伤。” 好莱坞媒体《每日野兽》称，有消息人士向他们透露，是两人的女儿罗米最先发现他们倒在血泊中；罗伯·莱纳当时已死亡，妻子米歇尔在救护车送院途中离世。 此外，《人物》杂志称通过多方消息，得知莱纳夫妇系被他们的儿子尼克（Nick）所杀害。不过，这一说法并未获得警方的证实。罗伯·莱纳与摄影师米歇尔·辛格相识于《当哈利遇到莎莉》拍摄时期，两人于1989 年结婚，育有三个子女，分别为杰克（Jake）、尼克（Nick）和罗米（Romy）。 2014年，罗伯·莱纳与妻子偕三名子女杰克、罗米、尼克（右三至右一）出席活动。 《人物》杂志还在报道中指出：尼克2016年接受其采访时，曾谈到自己长达数年的毒品成瘾经历。这段经历始于他十几岁出头，导致他一度流落街头。他表示，大约从15岁开始，便反复进出戒毒康复机构；随着成瘾问题不断加重，他逐渐与家人疏远，并在多个州经历了长时间的无家可归生活。 2025年9月15日，罗伯·莱纳在纽约出席活动。视觉中国 图 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

### 演员何晴追悼会举行，其子追思母亲：北京这场雪像是为她而下
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-15 06:53 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178536
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178536

一场雪落，人间倩影化雪归天。 12月15日上午，众多剧迷粉丝冒着严寒赶到北京昌平殡仪馆久安厅，送别演员何晴最后一程。12月13日，这位被誉为“古典第一美人”的演员因病去世，终年61岁。 不到10点，殡仪馆告别厅外已经站满了前来悼念的观众和粉丝，有人胸前佩戴小白花，有人手捧鲜花，一位浙江的网友还托人送来了悼念花圈。 “何晴的作品在我们心中留下了太多美好回忆，她的演技和性格都让我们深深喜爱，这次听到她突然去世的消息，我们非常意外，来到这里也是一种悼念。”一位何晴的影迷说。 现场粉丝在悼念簿上写下对何晴的话，不到一会儿，悼念簿就已写满对她的怀念。一位观众用清秀的字迹写下：“亲爱的何晴，我们的童年、青春都在您的影视作品中得到陪伴。美丽可人的何晴，很痛心听到您的消息，我代表我的同学们来这为你送行。” 曾在电视剧《水浒传》中饰演卢俊义的演员王卫国也来到现场，神色哀切。他说自己和何晴既是邻居，也是多年好友，在他印象中何晴是一个温婉、暖心的人，没有架子，总是远远地和人打招，笑嘻嘻地说话。何晴生病时常给王卫国打电话，请他送自己去医院。即便病重时，何晴也保持乐观积极的态度，王卫国有些事情想不开，她还来开导自己。“何晴走了，我们都很难过。只要你记住她，她就永远还在。”王卫国说。 《水浒传》中卢俊义的扮演者王卫国 《西游记》中万圣公主扮演者张青深情回忆何晴往事：“我们是小时候就认识的好朋友，从80年代到现在，有缘分做了这些年的朋友。她说话慢慢的，很甜很温柔。” 《西游记》中万圣公主扮演者张青 在广大观众的真挚请求下，原本仅面向亲友的告别仪式临时对外开放，大家排着队，秩序井然地进入灵堂，与这位“荧屏中的温婉佳人、生活中的坚韧女性”做最后的道别。 久安厅内的屏幕上滚动播放着何晴的照片，厅内四周摆满了亲友的花圈，其中包括六小龄童、唐国强、翁虹、尤勇智等何晴圈内好友送来的花圈，还有《三国演义》剧组送来的花圈。人群中不时传来一阵抽泣。 何晴之子许何代表亲友致悼词。他回忆了何晴对抗病魔的乐观积极，以及作为母亲对孩子深深的爱和眷恋。 许何说，妈妈很喜欢下雪，经常在雪后穿一件毛茸茸的衣服外出赏雪。“今年12月12日北京下了第一场雪，我摸着妈妈的脸跟她说北京下雪了，下得好大，好像很久都没有下过这么大的雪。在我的心里，这场雪好像是刻意为她下的。12月13日早晨天空晴朗，白色的雪布满了大地，我妈妈在她最喜欢的早晨离开了大家，去了天国，远离了所有的疾病和痛苦。” 何晴，1964年1月13日出生于浙江衢州江山市。她是中国内地唯一一位演遍四大名著影视作品的女演员，被誉为“古典第一美女”。

Click to expand Image Family members of fishermen wait for news at the harbor captaincy in Manta, Ecuador, on September 3, 2026, after the US military intercepted and sank a vessel. © 2026 Ariel Ochoa/AFP via Getty Images Between August 28 and September 16, US military forces intercepted and destroyed eight Ecuadorian fishing vessels, alleging that they served as floating refueling stations for drug-trafficking boats. They detained 140 of the 160 crew members and transferred them to Ecuadorian authorities, who charged 90 with “unlawful association.” Since Human Rights Watch reported on the operations, Ecuadorian courts have acquitted 40 people. In an October 29 judgment reviewed by Human Rights Watch, a Manta judge acquitted eight fishermen from a vessel named the Don Rufo. The prosecution’s own witnesses, including Ecuadorian police and Navy officials, testified that no illicit items were recovered, and that they knew of no prior investigation linking the fishermen to organized crime. The judge said the prosecution rested on a “chain of successive presumptions.

The so-called “vandals pay” bill is now pending review by the National Assembly. “Penalizing people engaged in their right to peaceful protest is the wrong answer to tackling violent disorder in France,” said Eva Cossé, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Lawmakers in both houses should reject this problematic bill entirely.” The bill was introduced by the government on September 16 under a fast-track procedure.

Security forces in the city of Yogyakarta on Java Island used rubber bullets, water cannons, and tear gas to disperse protesters, injuring several and detaining over 150 people, including children. Source: CEPR VoxEU

Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline

Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/inside-central-banks-currency-portfolios-new-evidence-149-countries-and-23-currencies

An increasing number of central banks have begun disclosing reserve currency shares. This column introduces a new public database providing information on the reserve currency composition of 149 countries across 23 currencies, covering the period 1999 to 2026, which allows a granular analysis of the factors driving reserve currency composition. Liquidity, return, and safety are the determinants most frequently cited when explaining allocation decisions. While central banks rarely acknowledge it publicly, a growing body of evidence also suggests a role for geopolitical considerations and international alliances.

### Currency risk drives remittance fees as much as markups do
Source: CEPR VoxEU
Published: 2026-11-16 00:00 UTC
URL: https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/currency-risk-drives-remittance-fees-much-markups-do
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:17 UTC

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/currency-risk-drives-remittance-fees-much-markups-do

Senders now have more ways than ever to move money across borders, yet costs remain high and vary widely across corridors. This column argues that a missing piece in explaining these high costs is the exchange rate risk borne by the intermediaries that move the currency, the money transfer operators. Across 339 remittance corridors worldwide, fees rise when the recipient country’s currency becomes more volatile, and this currency risk adds about as much to the price of a transfer as operators’ markups. Competition alone cannot lower these costs.

### The effects of inflation on euro area public debt
Source: CEPR VoxEU
Published: 2026-11-16 00:00 UTC

Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/effects-inflation-euro-area-public-debt

Whether inflation can ease public debt burdens is an increasingly important question as debt sustainability concerns rise in the euro area. This column applies a new debt decomposition framework to assess how inflation affected debt ratios in the five largest euro area sovereign issuers over 2005–2025. It finds that inflation played a small role in reducing the public debt burden. The post-pandemic inflation surprise largely reflected imported costs, which do little to raise nominal output. Increases in longer-term inflation compensation lowered the market value of debt, but were not sufficient to offset the debt-increasing effect of earlier declines.

Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/growth-alone-unlikely-fiscal-saviour-resolving-long-run-fiscal-tensions-oecd

In public discourse on fiscal tensions across OECD countries, the potential contribution of higher economic growth tends to be overstated. This column argues that long-run fiscal sustainability cannot prudently rely on growth alone. OECD modelling shows that under current policy settings, productivity-led growth provides minimal fiscal relief due to wage linkages, benefit indexation, and relative price effects. Growth from rising labour utilisation is fiscally more potent, but restraining public expenditure is the surest path to long-run fiscal sustainability.

### Macroeconomic effects of rare earth supply disruptions
Source: CEPR VoxEU
Published: 2026-11-14 00:00 UTC
URL: https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/macroeconomic-effects-rare-earth-supply-disruptions
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/macroeconomic-effects-rare-earth-supply-disruptions

The market for rare earth elements is relatively small in value, but shortages can lead to disproportionate output losses. This column introduces a network model to quantify the output losses from a large and permanent shortage of rare earth elements. At short horizons less than one year, GDP losses range from 0.6% in the UK to 1.5% in the US and 1.8% in Japan. Supply chain risk assessments need to incorporate production networks to understand the vulnerabilities from such disruptions. Policymakers should build strategic reserves and develop domestic capacity to help withstand the short-run losses from rare earth shortages.

### Inflation and the Polarisation of Reality
Source: CEPR VoxEU
Published: 2026-11-13 00:00 UTC
URL: https://cepr.org/multimedia/inflation-and-polarisation-reality
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/multimedia/inflation-and-polarisation-reality

In recent years, shoppers in Türkiye do not need the evening news to tell them prices have been rising, because they see it at the till. But the till only tells you about the history of inflation. When they turn on the television, the news might tell them what to expect next, and which channel they choose will matter. Orkun Saka (City St George's, University of London) and his co-authors matched a monthly household survey to the transcripts of prime-time news on 13 Turkish channels. He tells Tim Phillips about how the way a channel talks more about inflation, and how often it mentions the word, affects what viewers expect will happen next. Do polarised TV channels lead to a "polarisation of reality"?

### How Will the 340B Rebate Model Pilot Affect Covered Entity Finances? -- by Charles J. Courtemanche
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36006#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36006#fromrss

The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) plans to implement a pilot switching 340B from an upfront discount model to a rebate model for drugs in the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program (MDPNP). This study uses calibration methods to predict the impact of the rebate model pilot (RMP) on covered entities’ net revenues from the 340B program. I examine possible losses from averted duplicate discounts; denial of valid claims; manufacturers using data to exert influence; liquidity-related expenses; and administrative and staffing costs. I also project the effects of switching the entire 340B program to a rebate model. I project net revenue losses from the RMP of $1.5 billion. Expansion to all of 340B would increase the predicted losses to $22.8 billion, cutting net revenues from the program by 32%. The majority of losses will come from administrative and staffing costs, which do not benefit manufacturers, implying a net negative effect of switching to a rebate model.

### Horizontal Equity of Taxation: Citizen Beliefs and Policy Preferences -- by Pierre Bachas, Christopher A. Hoy, Anders Jensen, Mahvish Shaukat
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36007#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36007#fromrss

Taxes are harder to enforce on the self-employed than on wage earners, creating horizontal inequities among taxpayers with similar incomes. Using tax microsimulation and household survey data from 29 developing countries, we show that horizontal inequities in actual tax systems are comparable in magnitude to vertical equity and are exacerbated by progressive reforms that fall disproportionately on wage earners. We then conduct surveys and randomized information experiments in Pakistan to study public perceptions of these inequities. Although providing information raises fairness concerns, it does not increase support for reforms reducing it, revealing an important political constraint to improving tax equity.

### Monetary policy in a Phelps–Winter Economy -- by Bruce C. Greenwald, Joseph E. Stiglitz
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36008#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:17 UTC

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36008#fromrss

We use the Phelps-Winter customer market—providing a better theory of price determination for large parts of the economy than the standard model—to show that raising interest rates induces higher prices, as firms value current profits more, and are more willing to lose customers for short-term gains. These inflationary effects can be significant in relevant ranges of interest rates; they exist in the short run even when interest rate hikes succeed in cutting aggregate demand; and that they are amplified by policy uncertainty and the uncertainty about the effects of interest rate changes, both of which have increased as conventional policy has demonstrably failed badly to keep inflation at the 2% target. Empirical studies confirm this low level of ineffectiveness of raising interest rates in reducing inflation.

### Measuring the Impact of Impact Measurement -- by Emanuele Colonnelli, Timothy McQuade, Natalia Rigol, Benjamin N. Roth
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知

Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36009#fromrss

Impact measurement is central to impact investing and social entrepreneurship, yet little is known about whether firms benefit privately from measuring impact. We conduct the first randomized controlled trial of an impact measurement intervention among high-growth social enterprises in India. Treated firms exhibit nearly twice as much revenue growth and raise nearly twice as much capital as control firms. In a companion experiment with early-stage investors, we find that investors respond strongly to quantified impact metrics but not to generic qualitative impact statements. Together, our results show that impact measurement can shape firm growth and capital allocation.

### Gambling for Goals -- by Costas Arkolakis, Spencer Y. Kwon, Dominic Russel, Claire Shi, Hyunjoo Yang
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36010#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36010#fromrss

Young adults in advanced economies have grown more pessimistic about their economic prospects in recent years. At the same time, gambling-like financial activities have proliferated. We link these trends through a Friedman-Savage (1948) motive: when life goals such as homeownership or marriage seem out of reach, individuals turn to financial gambles. We test this theory using an original survey combined with millions of linked records from Korea’s leading credit bureau, telecom provider, and credit card issuer. Consistent with the theory, individuals who place greater importance on hard-to-reach goals take more risk, and the form of risk they take varies systematically with their distance from those goals. Within individuals, cryptocurrency app usage rises during unemployment and falls after winning the right to purchase price-regulated housing through a lottery. A calibration shows how hard-to-reach goals lead households to act more aggressively on their beliefs, amplifying the consequences of overoptimism.

### Investment and Governance: Through The Lens of Sustainability -- by Jitendra Aswani, Roberto Rigobon
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36011#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36011#fromrss

Using 3,944 sustainable bond issuances by public firms from 2013 to 2022, we examine the causal effect of sustainable investment on governance adoption. A heteroskedasticity-based identification strategy reveals that a 1% increase in sustainable debt (by total debt) raises the likelihood of sustainable governance adoption by 9.2%. Such adoption improves environmental performance by 16% (structural estimates). These effects are confined to non-financial firms; for financial firms, governance adoption alone is in-sufficient, as sustainable loan borrowers environmental performance does not improve. Firms with stronger environmental performance are less likely to adopt sustainable governance. Results are robust to alternative definitions and extensive specification checks.

Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · baseline

Attribution: LessWrong [public_ideas] https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/GSseMxyeJmqQgKQi4/the-siren-song-of-the-inside-game

BLUF: There’s a structural pull to overinvest in cosying up with frontier labs relative to publicly holding them to account. Now seems like a good time to rebalance. When thinking about influencing an organisation (like, say, a frontier lab), it’s useful to distinguish between the inside game and the outside game. The inside game means trying to work with the insiders: building trust and influence with them, and looking for compromises. The outside game means applying external pressure: building broad political will and being willing to take a more adversarial posture. In an ideal world, you do a mixture of the two: the good cop and the bad cop, the carrot and the stick, and so on. But AI safety does not have some single strategy. Instead, people self-sort based largely on local incentives and ambient pressures. And I think this disproportionately pulls towards the inside game.

Cross-posted from Oblomovka. The present moment rhymes with 1994 to me in many ways, and one of the clearest is in its compression of the future. In the Nineties, any act of forecasting or speculating about what was to come was always confounded by a brick wall, an energy barrier (of course, entirely spurious and manmade) at the year 2000. You’d move your finger across the smooth extrapolated lines of the present forwards, but your fingertips would always catch on that sharp boundary between the centuries. The twentieth century never thought of the twenty-first as anything other than impossibly distant — and suddenly it was upon us, and somehow all anyone’s visions could do was pile up at the end of the century. We all knew it wasn’t really the end of history, but we couldn’t see over that edge. The wall loomed. As a teenager, I assumed I’d be dead on or before Jan 1 2000. The twenty-first century was reserved for radioactive wastelands and alien conquests. Even as other walls fell, I couldn’t see any of us making it, until we counted down to zero, and nothing happened.

In 2024 we were posting about the astonishing progress in solar power. People were telling me, first of all, that fossil fuels were obsolete for electricity generation. And second, that for carbon-free electricity generation, nuclear couldn’t compete with solar. I had been converted to a solar believer by the growth of battery storage, but I was skeptical of the visions of Solartopia, where we run on solar all day and batteries all night. I think my skepticism has aged well, as data centers install natural gas turbines and hyperscalers work to restart nuclear plants. But the basis of my skepticism then was that batteries were being installed for a niche use, and that their price would have to drop substantially to escape that niche. Of course, the astonishing price drops in both solar and batteries are what made us all into solar believers. The hot graph we were all reposting was a “learning curve”, showing how price decreases as a function of cumulative production: how many watts of solar cells have ever been produced, or kWh of lithium-ion batteries.

tl;dr: You can use stacks of sheets with holes in them to visually verify moderately-large computations including widely used cryptographic hash functions, within human-scale timeframes. Imagine that all the world's computers have been taken over by an AI swarm. You don't know whether you can trust the AI swarm to be honest with you - you're skeptical, in part because it just took over all the world's computers, which doesn't seem like an act of a particularly trustworthy AI swarm. Here's the thing: you really need to run an important program you've written down. Maybe you need to check a cryptographically signed message from your spy friend. Or maybe you work in a map factory and you really need to figure out how many colors you need to color all the countries on your latest map. An AI tells you that it would be happy to run the program for you, but you think you heard it snickering behind your back. Is there any way you can trust the results it gives you?

In a nutshell Point 1: Safety isn't backdated on earlier models, todays Fable 5.2 will be trivial for someone in 2035 to jailbreak, but some capabilities will be just as deadly in 2035 as they are today, i.e. anything biological. Point 2: If nukes were available on every corner to every Jill and Joe, we'd be in ruins. Reactive, legal enforcement is not sufficient. Point 3: The fuzzy paradox where you have access to immense capabilities but minimal proactive safety mechanisms might be a sign we are living in a transitional period on AI safety. Point 4: Infufficient progress is being made in model safety, the clock runs as the probabilities a small group of idiots do something terrible increases. The core point: Future improvements may not be able to undo the proliferation of dangerous capabilities already released. Note: it doesn't need to be Fable 5.2, but an open source equivelent that appears next year. Old Models can be dangerous too, (or they soon will be) When I was playing about with old LLM models, it occured to me how easy they were to jail break.

College students are convenient guinea pigs. Living on the campuses of leading research institutions and easily enticed by gift cards and other one-off perks, they’re the most scientifically scrutinized humans in history, and studies involving college students regularly catalyze novel ideas for further research. One such idea, arising relatively recently, is the notion that sleeping consistently is more important than sleeping longer — for both restfulness and overall health. Irregular sleepers College students might be the perfect demographic for studying this concept, largely due to their erratic sleep schedules. A decade ago, Andrew J.K. Phillips and William M. Clerx, then sleep researchers at Harvard Medical School, recruited 63 full-time undergraduates at Harvard College for a study on sleep. Phillips and Clerx were curious whether sleep regularity, the day-to-day variability in sleep duration, onset time, wake time, or quality, could be linked to academic performance. Participants tracked their sleep via online diaries for a month.

Here in the Universe, there are a few things that are as close-to-perfect as can be. The Sun, for instance is the roundest object in the Universe, but other stars are rounder, with white dwarfs and neutron stars exhibiting even more perfectly roundness. Meanwhile, in terms of keeping time, we might think of the spinning Earth as a wonderful clock — after all, we base our calendar off of it — but the Earth spins down over time and changes its distance from the Sun: both factors that lead to it being rather imperfect as a timekeeper, especially over the long run. For keeping time, it turns out that the best natural clocks in the Universe are millisecond pulsars. It’s possible to look at a millisecond pulsar, measure its timing, and then look away for extremely long periods of time, like perhaps a year, and then when you return to it, know whether a billion pulses have elapsed or a billion-and-one pulses have elapsed.

Underneath the political map of Europe’s nation-states simmers another reality: a tangle of economic and logistical corridors that transcend national borders. The best known of these is the Blue Banana. Many others aren’t as visible, and that is due to poor marketing: They lack an equally imaginative handle. Hence this modest proposal: If the European Union is serious about integration, it should get silly about names. All 12 of its major transnational economic corridors should be named after the bendy fruit. In other words, Europe should go full bananas. “Looks like a banana,” said the minister The Blue Banana — the first of the bunch, so to speak — is of surprisingly recent vintage. First proposed in 1989 by French geographer Roger Brunet as an economic zone with common characteristics, this urban-industrial belt runs from Manchester in northern England to Milan in northern Italy. A French minister remarked that Brunet’s area looked a bit like a banana, an illustrator for Le Nouvel Observateur colored it blue, and hey presto, the Blue Banana was born.

Few literary canons inspire as much reverence, and fear, as Russia’s. The sheer size and complexity of novels like Leo Tolstoy’s War and Peace (1867) and Fyodor Dostoevsky’s The Brothers Karamazov (1880) have created two groups of readers: Those who have read them, and those who say they will read them — one day. For one reason or another, that day never seems to come. Allow us to make the case for why it should. Reading Russian literature is not only worth the effort, but is also far less arduous than many of us have been led to believe. For this guide, Big Think reached out to Rosamund Bartlett, a cultural historian, translator, and author of many books, among them Tolstoy: A Russian Life (2011) and Chekhov: Scenes from a Life (2004). An honorary research fellow at Oxford, she discusses what makes Russian literature so special and shares her personal reading recommendations. ### Ask Ethan: Can you write a beginner’s guide to the Standard Model?
Source: Big Think

Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Big Think [public_ideas] https://bigthink.com/starts-with-a-bang/beginners-guide-standard-model/

For thousands of years, humanity would wonder just what it was — at a fundamental, elementary level — that made up everything we saw, heard, or otherwise interacted with in the Universe. Ideas ran rampant early on, ranging from the notion of elements to a fundamental single root of everything to tiny building blocks composed of a variety of geometric shapes. It was only in the 19th century that we began breaking terrestrial matter down into the microscopic constituents that compose it, like molecules and atoms, that we began approaching the problem scientifically, and scientific progress continued into the 20th and now 21st centuries. Most of us learn in school about the existence of atoms, the different species of atom (known as elements), and the constituents of atoms: an atomic nucleus made of protons and neutrons, where the number of protons in the nucleus determines which element the atom is, and the much lower-mass electrons that orbit around the nucleus itself.

Attribution: MUBI Notebook [film_moving_image] https://mubi.com/en/notebook/posts/scene-report-summer-break-in-mexico-city

Scene Report is a series that explores a city's moviegoing culture over a month. Illustration by Angelo Dolojan. There are summers when Mexico City belongs to cinema. This was not one of them—it belonged to football. Months before the first whistle, sidewalks were being repaired with unusual urgency, facades were being repainted, metro stations acquired new signage, long-neglected public spaces suddenly became worthy of investment. Like every global mega-event, the FIFA World Cup arrived with the familiar rhetoric of urban renewal and international prestige. Whether those promises will outlast the tournament remains to be seen. What mattered during those weeks was that the city had accepted football as its temporary organizing principle. As someone who had deliberately decided to stay in Mexico City to experience the tournament, I surrendered without resistance. I have always loved football, and the chance to watch a World Cup unfold in my own city felt like a once-in-a-lifetime experience. During the tournament, everyday routines dissolved into celebration.

In this episode, the conversation explores the relationship between imagination and reality, and the boundary between images and truth. Federico Luis is an Argentine filmmaker who has directed nearly ten documentary and fiction short films. In 2019, he presented La siesta in the Official Short Film Competition at the Cannes Film Festival, a section he recently returned to, winning the Palme d’Or for his documentary Para los contrincantes (2026), filmed in Mexico. In 2024, he premiered his debut feature, Simon of the Mountain, at Cannes Critics’ Week, where it received the Grand Prize. The film subsequently screened at several other international festivals, including San Sebastián, Havana, Cairo and Biarritz. Through a filmography that, in different ways, unsettles, distorts and expands reality, Luis explores how the freedom of fantasy can lend an air of mystery to the most ordinary situations.

Attribution: MUBI Notebook [film_moving_image] https://mubi.com/en/notebook/posts/mubi-podcast-yol-the-picture-made-from-prison-with-alejandro-g-inarritu

How do you direct a Palme d’Or-winning film…from behind bars? Our new season about dissident filmmakers kicks off with the tale of Yilmaz Güney—one of Turkish cinema’s most revered and controversial directors—from his days as a tough-guy movie star nicknamed “The Ugly King,” to his years as a left-wing activist, to his 19-year prison sentence…during which he somehow managed to make his masterpiece, Yol (1982). Featuring Oscar-winner and Yol megafan Alejandro G. Iñárritu (Digger, 2026) and German-Turkish auteur Fatih Akin (Head-On, 2004). The MUBI Podcast returns for its 12th season, “Under Pressure.” At a time when artists worldwide are being threatened or stifled by their governments, host Rico Gagliano tells the stories of filmmakers from across history and around the world who have made movies in spite of incredible state pressure to compromise, give in, or give up. From 1970s Turkey to modern-day America, these are alternately wild, sobering, controversial, and inspiring tales of art by any means necessary.

Attribution: MUBI Notebook [film_moving_image] https://mubi.com/en/notebook/posts/the-possibilities-of-the-unseen-in-conversation-with-lee-chang-dong

Lee Chang-dong. When I first met Lee Chang-dong in person, in April 2025, he was already waiting for me at his office in Seoul’s Mapo District. He sat hunched over his notes, reviewing the questions I had sent him in advance. After a moment of small talk, he looked up at me, his expression suddenly serious. “How long do you want to talk?” he asked. I thought two hours would be enough. “Not enough,” he replied. We talked for nearly four hours, with a large Secret Sunshine (2007) poster looming behind us. Our conversation took place in Seoul ahead of a retrospective of Lee’s work at Poland’s New Horizons Film Festival. He couldn’t attend in person, as he was busy finishing Possible Love (2026), his first feature since Burning (2018). When we met again this fall to continue our conversation after the premiere of his long-awaited return to cinema, I understood just how right he had been. One conversation had not been enough. Talking to Lee feels like reading an essay as it takes shape; his answers have the texture of carefully composed speech.

To accompany his Global Ear feature in The Wire 514, Simon Coates compiles an annotated playlist of tracks from the Sri Lankan city Situated on Colombo’s Vauxhall Street, Musicmatters sits at the centre of the Sri Lankan city's experimental music world. “A lot of my introduction to experimentation in music came through Musicmatters around 2010,” says bass player Uvindu Perera. “I was new to it then, but these people were already listening widely and sharing references.” Simultaneously a collective, a school (Perera now teaches there), a record label and home to the Sound Room performance space, Musicmatters offers both an alternative to exam-heavy Western music education and provides space for explorations in sound as art and experimentation. Many of the musicians in this playlist have links to the organisation. Isuru Kumarasinghe “Time #1” From Ekāgra: Sitting With Trees Under Skies (Bandcamp) 2020 “Time #1” is taken from the 2020 album, Ekāgra: Sitting With Trees Under Skies, that formed the soundtrack to a video artwork Isuru Kumarasinghe made during the Covid lockdowns.

Attribution: The Wire Magazine [music_sound] https://www.thewire.co.uk/video/video-79994

Watch an exclusive clip of Turkish improv band ZeN’s Bakırköy Psychiatric Hospital concert from 1998 On 23 June 1998, Istanbul based experimental rock group ZeN performed at Bakırköy Psychiatric Hospital, following an invitation from two nurses who worked there. The musicians visited the hospital beforehand and decided to approach the performance with sensitivity to their audience while remaining true to their commitment to improvisation. At times, the lyrics seem to tell the story of the hospital and the concert itself, responding directly to the surroundings. The performance subsequently became one of the group’s most remarkable and cult recordings, released on cassette and CD in 1999 and reissued on vinyl in 2023. This exclusive edit with English subtitles is hosted by The Wire ahead of the release of a new documentary, ZeNistan, exploring the activities of ZeN throughout the 1990s.

### Against the Grain: Music criticism can become critical again – here's how
Source: The Wire Magazine
Published: 2026-11-09 00:00 UTC
URL: https://www.thewire.co.uk/in-writing/collateral-damage/against-the-grain-music-criticism-can-become-critical-again-here-s-how
Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · culture_probe
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Wire Magazine [music_sound] https://www.thewire.co.uk/in-writing/collateral-damage/against-the-grain-music-criticism-can-become-critical-again-here-s-how

Popular music criticism can become relevant again by situating itself in broader theoretical frameworks, argues Rafael Lubner in The Wire 514 These are lean times for popular music criticism. Negotiating a gutted publishing landscape, amid a Spotify-led devaluation of listening, the form finds itself under serious threat. One index of criticism’s attenuated state is the narrowing frame of reference employed by critics to apprehend musical objects – rarely do we find new works in the visual arts, film or literature employed to understand transformations in music’s sound or form. Take, as a point of comparison, Greg Tate’s recently reissued Flyboy In The Buttermilk (reviewed in The Wire 513). Here are passionate defences of Miles Davis’s earth-shaking mid-1970s funk odysseys alongside surveys of Afrodiasporic art and reviews of writer Nathaniel Mackey and literary critic Henry Louis Gates Jr. Contemporary music criticism, by contrast, seems resolutely committed to understanding music as siloed from the non-musical.

### From the Fun Palace to the Fish: Architecture’s Triumph or Computation’s Takeover?
Source: ArchDaily
Published: 2026-11-16 04:00 UTC
URL: https://www.archdaily.com/1188572/from-the-fun-palace-to-the-fish-architectures-triumph-or-computations-takeover
Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · culture_probe
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: ArchDaily [architecture_urbanism] https://www.archdaily.com/1188572/from-the-fun-palace-to-the-fish-architectures-triumph-or-computations-takeover

The Heydar Aliyev Center in Baku, Azerbaijan, rises in fluid curves and folds in the midst of a wide clearing in the city's gridded forest of urban blocks. The striking structure, completed in 2013 by Zaha Hadid Architects, acts as a primary venue for the country's cultural programs. Its curvaceous form sits in contrast to its rectilinear surroundings, marking its importance. The carefully curated curves epitomize a constant ambition in the studio's work–to dissolve the distinction between the horizontal and the vertical, between inside and outside, and between landscape and building. Needless to say, its complexity marks it as a feat of construction as well as of architecture. As Zaha Hadid Architects note, "Advanced computing allowed for the continuous control and communication of these complexities among the numerous project participants." Indeed, it is computing that made the building of the center possible, as well as other projects by the studio.

Attribution: Rock Paper Shotgun [games] https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/the-sunday-papers-836

While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist. Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose? Read more

Fuel breaks are linear strips of land along which vegetation is cleared or thinned—constructed along ridgelines, roads and other strategic places—to give firefighters a better chance to safely slow or steer a fire. Often described as "speed bumps" for wildfires, fuel breaks rarely stop fire spread on their own, but they do give crews critical anchor points for building firelines, setting backfires or safely applying water and retardant. They have been used since the 1960s across many landscapes.

A surprising new study suggests that when and how often older adults nap could reveal hidden warning signs about their health. Researchers followed 1,338 people for up to 19 years and discovered that longer, more frequent naps were linked to higher mortality, while morning nappers faced a 30% greater risk of death than afternoon nappers. ### Accessible 3D Printed Archimedes System for Accurate and Precise Density Measurements and Uncertainty Analysis
Source: arXiv
Published: 2026-11-16 05:00 UTC
URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17342
Source meta: preprint · primary · R4 · P5 · signal
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:18 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17342

arXiv:2611.17342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate and precise density measurements are important for characterizing solid materials and for evaluating physical properties that are strongly affected by porosity. While several methods are available for determining density, measurements of small or irregularly shaped samples can be limited by sample geometry, balance precision, liquid density, and other experimental sources of uncertainty. In this study, an accessible Archimedes density measurement system was developed using 3D printed components and an analytical balance for the measurement of solid and liquid densities. The measurement of solid densities requires knowing the exact density of the liquid. Therefore, copper, vanadium, and indium standards were used to measure the densities of ethanol (0.8116 +/- 0.0005 g/cm3), distilled water (0.9982 +/- 0.0013 g/cm3), and hexanes (0.6748 +/- 0.0016 g/cm3), all of them showing strong agreement with literature values.

### Curvature-Aware Edge Dynamic GNNs for Low-$p_T$ Track Reconstruction at HL-LHC
Source: arXiv
Published: 2026-11-16 05:00 UTC
URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17343
Source meta: preprint · primary · R4 · P5 · signal
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:18 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17343

arXiv:2611.17343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Particle track reconstruction in high-energy collider experiments is a computationally demanding combinatorial problem, traditionally solved by Kalman filters that scale poorly with increasing detector occupancy. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative. In this work, we introduce the Manifold Helical-IN, a novel Interaction Network architecture that explicitly embeds detector spacepoints onto a helical manifold chart using curvature-aware features. This geometric projection mathematically unrolls the tightly curling trajectories of low-momentum particles. Consequently, the network can distinguish true physical tracks from combinatorial noise with good precision. Evaluated on the TrackML challenge dataset, the proposed Manifold Helical-IN achieves a reconstruction efficiency of 0.9675 in the experimentally critical $p_T > 0.5$ GeV regime, approaching recently reported Transformer-based approaches. Crucially, the manifold embedding yields a fake track rate of 0.0037.

### Rank-One Ultralight Dark Matter Response in a Full-Tensor Gravity Gradiometer
Source: arXiv
Published: 2026-11-16 05:00 UTC
URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17344
Source meta: preprint · primary · R4 · P5 · signal
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:18 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17344

arXiv:2611.17344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A full-tensor superconducting gravity gradiometer whose four test masses carry two compositions in a $2+2$ pattern acquires a composition-dependent channel for dilaton-coupled ultralight dark matter. The reconstructed response is the rank-one tensor $\K=\gv_\phi(t)\otimes\qv$, with the axis of $\qv$ fixed in advance by the material assignment, and obeys the parameter-free null condition $\K(\mathbf{I}-\Pq)=0$, which no gravity gradient or platform rotation alone can satisfy; it vanishes for a single composition. For copper and lead, the sensitivity reaches $d_{\hat m}-d_g\simeq3.4\times10^{-8}$, and $4.9\times10^{-10}$ with upgraded accelerometers.

### Composition-dependent ultralight dark matter detection with a tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometer
Source: arXiv
Published: 2026-11-16 05:00 UTC
URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17345
Source meta: preprint · primary · R4 · P5 · signal
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:18 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17345

arXiv:2611.17345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometers designed as full-tensor gravitational-wave detectors, such as the ground-based mSOGRO design and the proposed lunar LANGO observatory, reconstruct the acceleration-gradient tensor from four test masses. We show that giving the four test masses two compositions in a $2+2$ arrangement adds a composition-dependent ultralight dark matter (ULDM) channel to that same tensor readout, with no separate dark-matter sensor and no dark-matter-specific readout. A coherently oscillating scalar accelerates each mass in proportion to its dilaton charge, and the tensor reconstruction leaves the charges only in a mean, rejected with the common mode, and a single vector $\qv$ proportional to the charge contrast $\Delta\abaralpha_{AB}$ between the two materials. The response is the rank-one tensor $\K_{\ULDM}(t)=\gv_\phi(t)\otimes\qv$, whose amplitude is set by the halo, independent of $m_\phi$.

### Artificial Intelligence for VAMOS++: From Data Analysis to Intelligent Instrumentation
Source: arXiv
Published: 2026-11-16 05:00 UTC
URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17346
Source meta: preprint · primary · R4 · P5 · signal
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:18 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17346

arXiv:2611.17346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing complexity of nuclear-physics experiments calls for analysis methods that combine precision, efficiency, and reproducibility. This article reviews the integration of artificial intelligence into the analysis framework of the VAMOS++ large-acceptance magnetic spectrometer at GANIL and discusses its evolution toward intelligent instrumentation. Deep neural networks exploit nonlinear correlations between detector observables to reconstruct ion trajectories and identify atomic charge states and atomic numbers. These approaches achieve performance comparable to or better than conventional methods while substantially reducing manual intervention and processing time. Trajectory reconstruction reaches processing rates of millions of events per second, while particle identification using fractionally labelled events reduces analysis procedures from months or years to minutes.

arXiv:2611.17347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: R\&D on different gas-filled detectors such as Gas Electron Multipliers (GEMs), Resistive Plate Chambers (RPCs) and straw tubes has been carried out in the detector laboratory of Bose Institute for more than a decade, keeping in mind present and future high-energy physics experiments. In this article, performance studies of a single-mask triple-GEM detector using a $^{55}$Fe X-ray source with an Ar/CO$_2$ (70/30) gas mixture are described. The study focuses mainly on the gain, energy resolution, count rate, and stability of the chamber under long-term irradiation. The experimental setup, methodology, and analysis results are presented.

by Fang Wang, Hailan Yang Background Although China has made major advances in maternal health, city-level epidemiological evidence on maternal mortality remains scarce. Using maternal surveillance data from Taiyuan (2016–2024), we assessed trends in the maternal mortality ratio (MMR), examined causes of death, and identified associated factors to inform region-specific strategies for reducing MMR. Methods We extracted and validated data on maternal deaths and live births from the Taiyuan Municipal Maternal and Child Health Annual Reports. MMR was calculated per 100,000 live births. Poisson regression was used to examine temporal trends, and chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests were used for between-group comparisons. Analyses were stratified by geographic region, cause of death, and place of death; the study period was divided into three phases (2016–2018, 2019–2021, 2022–2024) for subgroup analysis. Results Between 2016 and 2024, Taiyuan recorded 424,392 live births and 33 maternal deaths, yielding an overall MMR of 7.76 per 100,000 live births (95% CI 5.35 to 10.92).

by Shengting Shi, Haokun Tong, Jingxuan Zhou, Zhanpeng Ji, Xinlei Zhang The susceptibility of loess to water-induced deterioration poses a major threat to geotechnical stability. This study investigates the small-strain dynamic behavior of loess treated with tremella fuciformis polysaccharide (TFP), a sustainable biopolymer, using resonant column tests. The evolution of the maximum shear modulus (Gmax) and reference shear strain (γr) was systematically analyzed under varying applied confining pressures, water contents, and TFP dosages. Results show that for untreated loess, Gmax follows a power-law growth with confining pressure and linear attenuation with water content. TFP treatment significantly bolsters the small-strain shear stiffness; at a 2% dosage (σc = 150 kPa, w = 13%), Gmax increases from 63.12 MPa to 139.93 MPa. TFP treatment enhances the initial shear stiffness while altering the reference shear strain, indicating changes in the strain-dependent modulus reduction characteristics.

by Daria L. Manalo, Jude Karlo G. Bolivar, Jeromir G. Bondoc, Blanca J. Nagataki, Karl Ian T. Ermino, Kazunori Kimitsuki, Leilanie B. Nacion, Mark Joseph M. Espino, Chun-Ho Park, Satoshi Inoue Rabies remains a major public health concern in endemic settings, where effective control depends on timely and reliable post-mortem confirmation of infection in animal reservoirs. Although the direct fluorescent antibody test (dFAT) remains the reference standard, its dependence on fresh brain tissue and susceptibility to specimen degradation limits its operational use in decentralized surveillance systems. The present findings demonstrate that the locally optimized RT-qPCR assay targeting the nucleoprotein gene in non-brain tissues exhibits high analytical sensitivity and strong concordance with dFAT results obtained from post-mortem brain specimens of dogs.

by Qiao Wei, Haiyan Song, Li Jiang, Xiuqin Li, Jihua Zhu Background Emphysema is a significant public health issue. Physical activity (PA) has been suggested to be associated with respiratory health; however, the relationship between PA intensity and emphysema remains insufficiently characterized. Methods This cross-sectional study utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2007 to 2016. Emphysema was defined based on self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to examine the association between different levels of PA and the odds of self-reported emphysema among older adults, adjusting for demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Results Higher levels of physical activity, particularly ≥3000 MET-minutes per week, were associated with lower odds of self-reported emphysema. A dose–response relationship was observed, with increasing PA levels associated with progressively lower odds of self-reported emphysema.

The world has never been wealthier. Yet in 2025, an estimated 831 million people lived on less than US$3 per day. This stark disparity exposes a systemic failure to translate global prosperity into basic security and opportunity for all. As slowing economic growth and multiple crises, such as conflict and climate change, undermine the momentum of global poverty reduction, governments now face a pressing test: whether they will still find, reach, and protect those already furthest behind, or allow them to fall deeper into poverty.

Mahmoudi et al. show here that contingency degradation is resistant to spontaneous recovery and reinstatement and that its learning, but not retrieval, depends on the lateral orbitofrontal cortex. Humanity is quickly starting to saturate our ability to track all of the satellites we have in deep space. NASA’s Deep Space Network (DSN) has been the workhorse for tracking such things for decades, but is quickly being overwhelmed by the number of requests it receives. Which in turn makes it harder to track some of the missions that have been launched recently. A new paper, available in pre-print on arXiv, from Ian Down, James McElreath, and Manoranjan Majji, of Advanced Space, Space Exploration Engineering, and Texas A&M respectively, offer a no-cost solution to that tracking problem - use solar array data from a spacecraft’s eclipse to determine where it is.

Researchers at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) have discovered a previously unknown specialized organelle structure in a deep-sea mollusk living at cold seeps in the South China Sea. Dedicated to maintaining bacterial symbiosis, this newly identified survival mechanism provides new insights into how deep-sea organisms adapt to nearly oxygen-free environments and opens new directions for research on chemosymbiosis, organelle evolution and deep-sea ecosystems.

Tiny skeletal plates recovered beside fossil whale bones in southern Denmark offer a rare glimpse of life around a whale carcass approximately 9.5 million years ago. Researchers have identified a new species of brittle star, Ophiura huebnerjenseni, from the Gram Clay Pit and suggest it represents the first fossil record of brittle stars associated with a whale fall.

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Microsoft Research Blog [ai_systems] https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/formally-verifying-agent-written-full-stack-web-apps-with-pdd-kit/

AI agents can generate code at a scale that’s hard for humans to review line-by-line. PDD Kit helps ensure the code is doing what the developer intended by creating formal specifications and testing against them. It converts developer intent into a Verus specification, proves AI-generated code meets it for every input, and uses tests where proofs aren't practical. Developers review intent, not every line. The post Formally verifying agent-written full-stack web apps with PDD Kit appeared first on Microsoft Research.

### Gödel's Notebooks in Obscure Shorthand Contain Myriad of Novel Proofs
Source: SoylentNews
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://soylentnews.org/article.pl?sid=26/11/14/1321220&from=rss
Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Updated: 2026-11-16 08:30 UTC

Fetch status: ok

JoeMerchant writes: https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026/nov/13/kurt-godel-notebooks-ai-helps-unlock-hidden-discoveries-man-who-transformed-maths With the help of Claude model LLM agents and the proof assistant Coq, logician Jan von Plato uncovered 663 theorems obscured in Kurt Gödel's 1940s shorthand notebooks, including roughly 400 verified proofs and 200 repairable ones. Most notably, the analysis revealed that Gödel was just one step away from proving the independence of the axiom of choice—a foundational breakthrough in set theory that later earned Paul Cohen the 1966 Fields Medal. Beyond confirming Gödel's past claims, the workbooks contain dozens of results that anticipated mathematical developments of the 1970s and 1980s, along with 14 entirely unexplored themes in logic and the foundations of mathematics. These discoveries build on Gödel's legacy of transforming modern mathematics and computation, demonstrating how his systematic, idea-driven proofs laid groundwork that researchers are only now beginning to explore.

### C++26 Stumbles at Finish Line Over Contracts Dispute
Source: SoylentNews
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://soylentnews.org/article.pl?sid=26/11/14/1319214&from=rss
Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Updated: 2026-11-16 03:47 UTC
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:18 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: SoylentNews [computing_cultures] https://soylentnews.org/article.pl?sid=26/11/14/1319214&from=rss

"Arthur T Knackerbracket" writes: ISO working group faces a fight over runtime checks, complexity, and the language's release timetable: The next version of the C++ programming language may be delayed at the last minute due to a dispute over a security-enhancing Contracts feature. Contracts have deeply split C++ technical maintainers. One group backs the C++ creator Bjarne Stroustrup, who is against the technology in its present form in grounds it was hastily implemented. But others are eager to see Contracts implemented, even arguing the tech's detractors are poisoning the C++ development process itself. The disagreement boiled over just before a vote to ratify the new version of the language. In October, the Draft International Standard (DIS) of C++26 failed its ISO ballot — the next-to-last stage in the International Organization for Standardization's approval process during which a standard's technical details are formally ratified by a set of national standards bodies.

Release: datasette-maplibre 0.1a0 The first new Datasette geospatial plugin in quite a while! This one combines the excellent MapLibre GL library with OpenFreeMap, the free vector map server operated by Zsolt Ero (you should sponsor Zsolt on GitHub.) I built most of this with a single prompt to Claude Fable 5.2: Look at datasette-cluster-map and datasette-leaflet-geojson plugins, then look at ~/dev/tools/openfreemap-demo.html - then build a brand new Datasette plugin that uses maplibreGL and openfreemap and combines the features of those other two plugins - but be creative and think outside the box for other useful features the plugin might have "Be creative and think outside the box" resulted in a few neat ideas - my favorite is that it displays SVG previews of GeoJSON shapes, then loads a WebGL preview only when they scroll into view. I also had Claude build a comprehensive demo which works in the latest Datasette Lite, so you can visit this link to load the plugin and a demo database in your browser via Pyodide and WebAssembly.

Attribution: Simon Willison's Weblog [computing_cultures] https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/15/datasette/

Release: datasette 1.0a43 I've been leaning hard into Claude Fable 5.2 to help knock things off the 1.0 milestone, which is now 53% complete. The biggest 1.0 item in this release is streaming support for output renderers - the built-in TSV and CSV export mechanisms now use this as well, and plugins can register themselves as capable of streaming every row in a table in one go via the new Response.stream() method. There are a couple of security fixes, one of which I deemed deserving of a GitHub advisory: private stored queries could be exposed, granting access to the title and SQL of the query (but not allowing that query to be executed). There are dozens of smaller improvements. The row page JSON representation finally has a design suitable for 1.0. A new Web Component provides copy-schema in various places. JSON in columns on the row page can be pretty-printed. There's a new DatasetteModal.confirm() JavaScript utility method. Plus dozens of bug fixes, including contributions by Zihan Dai, Peter Olkhovets, Ilya Khalafi, and Ankita Advitot.

Arthur t Knackerbracket writes: Now enables backup by default and hints a little on-prem infra never hurt anyone: Russian cloud operator Yandex has admitted to data loss after a drone attack on one of its datacenters. The attack, which Ukrainian press said was ordered by Kyiv, happened in early October and caused a fire and subsequent outage at Yandex's ru-central1-b availability zone. Subsequent strikes targeted more Yandex datacenters and disrupted more of the company's cloud and payment services. On Tuesday, Yandex posted an update on its recovery efforts, which it spun as something of a triumph because it restored over 97 percent of customer data. Of course that also means the company lost 2.84 percent of customer data, which it blamed on "critical hardware damage and a lack of backups on the platform." It's unclear if Yandex's use of the phrase "on the platform" indicates it doesn't keep backups of its own cloud, if whatever resilience techniques it employs don't create multiple copies of customer data, or if clients didn't protect their data.

Arthur t Knackerbracket writes: And find they were right all along: The image of the red ring around the black hole M87, produced by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) array, made front-page news around the world in 2019. There was one problem: there was a slim chance the depiction might be wrong. This week, a small team of four Australian researchers have published their work confirming the result based on a new machine learning algorithm using the same base data. The 2019 Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) image came from hundreds of scientists working together to capture the first direct view of a black hole's shadow. The measurements were taken at eight telescopes around the world, at locations including Chile, the US, and Antarctica. Reconstructing the image from the data so geographically distant meant instrument and environment errors could influence the accuracy of the resulting image. Potentially, alternative analyses of the data could have reconstructed an image without the iconic ring shape.

Arthur t Knackerbracket writes: https://www.engadget.com/2313187/grok-build-leaked-sensitive-spacexsi-data/ A flaw in SpaceXSI's Grok Build vibe-coding agent allowed sensitive data to leak from thousands of users including... SpaceXSI, security fraud firm Claroc told Ars Technica. The way Grok handles links to apps allowed them to be exposed publicly by certain types of DNS services, according to the security team. As a result, sensitive information involving employees was leaked out from a hospital group, a fire department and SpaceXSI itself. "We were shocked," the researchers wrote in a blog post. "The company that makes Grok had its own internal material open to anyone holding the link." The company called pages like that GhostShares, since they can be found and opened by people who were never given the link. Some of the material found from SpaceXSI included an onboarding plan, sales territory map of 594 strategic accounts, eight X advertising proposals, four live advertiser account boards and two copies of an X brand safety playbook.

Release: datasette-llm 0.1a11 datasette-llm is the intermediate plugin for Datasette that supports configuring LLMs for use with other Datasette plugins. This release adds support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so you can configure Datasette to use an LLM hosted anywhere that talks the OpenAI pseudo-standard web protocol. This means that if you're running local models with LM Studio or Ollama or llama.cpp (which just hit v1.0.0) you can run Datasette via uvx like this: wget https://datasette.io/content.db uvx --with datasette-agent datasette \ --root --secret 1 \ -s plugins.datasette-llm.default_model '{ "model": "lmstudio-qwen", "model_name": "qwen/qwen3.8-27b", "api_base": "http://localhost:1234/v1" }' content.db And you'll get a local server running a Datasette Agent instance powered by your local model! Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:18 UTC

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: LWN.net [computing_cultures] https://lwn.net/Articles/1107473/

Christoph Hellwig has announced the initial public release of XRAID—declustered parity RAID that is integrated into XFS. The two primary aims of XRAID are to support parity RAID on zoned devices like SMR hard drives, and to provide a fast RAID implementation without inherent data integrity problems. XRAID, just like zoned XFS also works on conventional hard drives and SSDs. Optimizing for SSD performance has not been a focus, but even without that, writes are up to 20 times faster than mdraid. [...] Work on XRAID has been ongoing for a year and a half, and while we aren't anywhere near ready for an upstream submission, we are interested in feedback and testing from a wider audience now. The current implementation supports zero to 2 parities. We did experiments with the SnapRAID parity library to support 3 and more parities, and while that is not included in the current version, support for more parities is planned and the code is prepared for it. The xfsprogs branch includes mkfs support and a new "xraid" utility for managing devices and inspecting an XRAID file-systems.

Patrick Garrity of VulnCheck has written a blog post that looks at vulnerabilities found by Anthropic's Project Glasswing since it launched on April 7, and finds it wanting: Of the 37,966 findings Anthropic reports, only 7,349 (19.4%) have been made public. Just 217 of those have been marked fixed. The more glaring number is that 4.4% (1,654) of the project's findings have already been marked as duplicates, 7.5x more duplicates than fixes. On top of that, 419 findings have been withdrawn. It seems odd that the ledger now claims a 94.2% true positive rate, up from 90.8% at launch, when more findings have been withdrawn or marked as duplicates than fixed, likely a feedback loop missing to the triage rates listed as "True Positives". [...] AI is a valuable tool for finding vulnerabilities, and I'm not discounting that. But seven months in, the evidence still doesn't match the launch narrative.

### Bliki: Generated Glossary
Source: Martin Fowler
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://martinfowler.com/bliki/GeneratedGlossary.html
Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R5 · P5 · baseline
Updated: 2026-11-12 14:15 UTC
Fetched: 2026-11-16 13:18 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Martin Fowler [computing_cultures] https://martinfowler.com/bliki/GeneratedGlossary.html

When we use LLMs in a specialized domain, such as the operations of any reasonably-large organization, there is a lot of specialized vocabulary. Such words and specialized meanings will be foreign to an LLM because they aren't in its training set, making it harder for the LLM to be effective when doing tasks in that domain. One technique to aid this is to use an LLM to generate a glossary of the terminology in that domain, and make this glossary available for any LLMs doing work in those circumstances. The sources for the LLM can be any material within the organization concerned such as documents, emails, and chat logs. In some cases getting transcripts of audio or video may be helpful, although most organizations generate enough text to do the job. The glossary-generating LLM should look for single words, and phrases of several words that regularly hang out together to form a meaningful term. The generator should be asked to identify terms that are new to it, but also known terms that are being used in unfamiliar ways. The latter can often cause the most confusion.

Automated testing in the age of AI coding assistants is problematic: when AI agents write both production and test code, developers risk losing the assurance that automated tests protect against functional errors. Matteo Vaccari makes three claims: (1) when AI writes the code, developers become its customers; (2) therefore customer tests, not developer tests, become the primary contract between humans and AI; (3) moving that contract into test data rather than test code makes it easier to protect it from unexpected modifications by coding agents. All of this optimizes for human-readable tests that establish a contract between humans and AI. While in the past DSL parsers and custom test runners were expensive to write and maintain, now AI makes them cheap. more…
